5258.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₂enǵʰ- (“to constrict”). Cognates include Old English enge (whence the first element in English hangnail), Latin angō, Sanskrit अंहु (áṃhu), and Old Armenian անձուկ (anjuk, “narrow; tight”).

5241.t: Generally considered to be a derivation in "-λ-" of ὀστέον (ostéon, “bone”), but this cannot be correct. According to Beekes, it is probably a Pre-Greek word.

5251.t: From ἀ- (a-) + ὁρατός (horātós, “seen”), verbal adjective of ὁράω (horáō).

5245.t: From ἀτενής (atenḗs, “intent”) + -ίζω (-ízō, denominative verb suffix), from τείνω (teínō, “to strain, to exert”).

5270.t: Generally taken as deriving from ἀ- (a-, “not”) + σφάλλω (sphállō, “to fall, cast down”), under the assumption that it denoted the material that protects walls from tumbling down.

5246.t: According to De Vaan, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ét(i). Compare Tocharian B ate (“away”).

5204.t: From ἀντίος (antíos): the adverb/preposition is from the adverbial accusative, and the noun is from the neuter singular.

5269.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *né Proto-Indo-European *n̥- Proto-Hellenic *ə- Ancient Greek ἀ- (a-) Ancient Greek σύλη (súlē) Ancient Greek -ος (-os) Ancient Greek ἄσυλος From ἀ- (a-, “without”) + σύλη (súlē, “seizure, plunder”).

5256.t: From ἀγάλλομαι (agállomai, “to be proud, exult in”) + -μα (-ma).

5250.t: Loaned from a non-Indo-European source, possibly Semitic (compare Aramaic עקיק). The river Ἀχάτης in Sicily is probably named after the mineral.

5266.t: From Proto-Hellenic *ároura, from the Proto-Indo-European heteroclitic noun *h₂érh₃-wr̥ ~ *h₂r̥h₃-wén-s, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂erh₃-.

5235.t: A loanword from Biblical Hebrew עירבון / עֵרָבוֹן (ʿērāḇōn, “guarantee, deposit”), or from a common third source, probably Semitic.

5233.t: From ἀποδείκνυμι (apodeíknūmi, “to show, display”) + -σις (-sis, verbal noun suffix).

5283.t: From ἐν- (en-, “in”) + χρίω (khrī́ō, “to rub, smear; anoint”).
